lesenParts.text: Last summer, I decided to do something completely different. Instead of spending my holidays at home, I signed up for a volunteer program in a small village in the Peruvian Andes. I had always wanted to travel, but I wanted to do more than just visit tourist sites; I wanted to make a real difference. When I arrived, I was surprised by how different everything was. The air was thin, the mountains were breathtaking, and the local community was incredibly welcoming. My main job was to help build a new classroom for the primary school. I had never held a hammer or painted a wall before, but the local builders were very patient with me. They taught me how to mix cement and how to work as part of a team. It was hard physical work, especially in the heat, but I felt a great sense of achievement every evening. In the afternoons, I helped the children with their English homework. They were so eager to learn, and we often spent hours laughing as we tried to communicate through gestures and simple words. Living without electricity and limited internet access was a challenge at first. I missed my friends and the comforts of home, but as the weeks passed, I realized that I didn't need those things to be happy. I learned to appreciate the simple things, like a shared meal or a beautiful sunset over the peaks. This experience changed my perspective on life. I realized that we don't need much to be happy, and that helping others is one of the most rewarding things you can do. I returned home with a new sense of purpose and a promise to myself that I would continue volunteering in the future. I have already started looking for local opportunities in my own city.

horenParts.instruction: Listen and answer the questions in Part 3.
horenParts.transcript: Hello everyone. I am here to tell you about the exciting changes coming to our local library next month. First, we are introducing a new online reservation system. You will be able to book books from home using your library card number. We are also opening a new study area on the second floor, which will be equipped with ten high-speed computers. For those who enjoy reading outside, we are launching a 'Books in the Park' scheme where you can borrow items from a mobile stand near the fountain. Please note that the library will be closed for renovations on the 15th of July. If you need help with your digital skills, we are starting free weekly workshops every Wednesday morning. Finally, if you have any suggestions, please leave a note in the suggestion box located next to the main entrance.

horenParts.instruction: Listen and answer the questions in Part 4.
horenParts.transcript: Interviewer: Today we are talking to Sarah Jenkins, who designs video games for a living. Sarah, was it always your dream to work in this industry? Sarah: Actually, no. I studied architecture at university. I loved drawing buildings, but I found the work a bit slow. One day, a friend showed me how to code a simple game, and I was hooked. I realized that game design is like architecture, but you can build entire worlds that people can interact with. Interviewer: That sounds fascinating. What is the most challenging part of your job? Sarah: People think it is just playing games all day, but it is actually very stressful. We have strict deadlines. If the game isn't ready for the holiday season, the company loses a lot of money. Sometimes I spend 12 hours a day staring at code. Interviewer: Do you ever get tired of it? Sarah: Sometimes, but then I see someone playing a game I helped create, and their face lights up. That feeling is worth all the hard work. Interviewer: What advice would you give to young people wanting to enter the field? Sarah: Don't just play games—learn how they are made. Start with simple tools and don't be afraid to make mistakes. Your first game will probably be terrible, and that is perfectly fine!

I'm planning to bring my camera, but what else do you think I should pack? Let me know if you have any other ideas for activities!' Notes: 1. Say you love the mountain idea. 2. Choose train (faster). 3. Suggest packing a warm jacket. 4. Suggest visiting the local lake.
